name: VA-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by about six points on the PVI
Subramanyam holds a massive fundraising advantage ($1.17M raised vs ~$107K)
Prediction markets price Democratic win odds at 95-97%
First-term incumbent with no serious outside spending against him
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Subramanyam: a D+6 district, incumbency, and a fundraising edge of more than ten-to-one, while markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price him near certain to win. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict that picture, the forecast stays at Safe D.
model.watch: A late surge of outside Republican spending or an unexpectedly strong national GOP environment could narrow the margin, though an outright upset remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northern Virginia's 10th District leans Democratic by about six points, and first-term incumbent Suhas Subramanyam is seeking reelection with the advantages that come with the seat. He has raised over $1.1 million and holds roughly $583,000 on hand, while Republican Dave Beckwith has raised about $107,000 with $54,000 available. No outside groups have spent against the incumbent, and no independent or third-party polling of the race is available.

Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price Subramanyam as a heavy favorite, with implied win probabilities in the mid-to-high 90s. With no expert ratings or polls to weigh, the forecast rests on the district's partisan lean, the incumbent's financial dominance, and market pricing, all of which point the same direction.
